numbering: IEEE first appearance in the current concise report
scope: External academic and professional references; original supplied model is the sole comparison baseline.

entries.title: You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection
entries.venue: IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
entries.ieee_entry: J. Redmon, S. Divvala, R. Girshick, and A. Farhadi, “You only look once: Unified, real-time object detection,” in Proc. IEEE Conf. Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), 2016, pp. 779–788, doi: 10.1109/CVPR.2016.91.
entries.supported_claim: The original YOLO formulates object detection as a single network that predicts bounding boxes and class probabilities from a complete image.
entries.limitation: This historical detector paper does not document the current pose implementation, its two-point output, or the accuracy of the cassette models.

supports: DOI in indexed primary IEEE record

entries.title: Ultralytics YOLO26
entries.ieee_entry: Ultralytics, “Ultralytics YOLO26,” Ultralytics Docs. Accessed: Nov. 28, 2026. [Online]. Available: https://docs.ultralytics.com/models/yolo26/
entries.supported_claim: YOLO26 is a model family with detection and pose-estimation variants.
entries.limitation: Current model documentation does not establish the accuracy of the project-specific checkpoint.

entries.title: ObjectLab: Automated Diagnosis of Mislabeled Images in Object Detection Data
entries.venue: ICML Workshop on Data-centric Machine Learning Research
entries.ieee_entry: U. Tkachenko, A. Thyagarajan, and J. Mueller, “ObjectLab: Automated diagnosis of mislabeled images in object detection data,” in ICML Workshop on Data-centric Machine Learning Research, 2023. [Online]. Available: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.00832
entries.supported_claim: ObjectLab uses model predictions to prioritize images that may contain missing, misplaced, or incorrectly classified bounding-box annotations for human review.
entries.limitation: A model-generated suspicion is not proof that an annotation is wrong; independent image inspection is still required, and the paper does not validate the project's corner labels.
metadata_notes: No proceedings page range was verified, so none is supplied.
The arXiv DOI is not represented as a publisher proceedings DOI.

entries.title: Noise-Aware Evaluation of Object Detectors
entries.venue: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
entries.ieee_entry: J. Murrugarra-Llerena and C. R. Jung, “Noise-aware evaluation of object detectors,” in Proc. IEEE/CVF Winter Conf. Applications of Computer Vision (WACV), 2025, doi: 10.1109/WACV61041.2025.00903.
entries.supported_claim: Bounding-box annotation uncertainty can alter detector evaluation, particularly for small objects and restrictive overlap thresholds, motivating sensitivity analysis of disputed references.
entries.limitation: This does not justify moving reference annotations toward a preferred model's predictions or treating model agreement as ground truth.

supports: author names as printed on paper
DOI in indexed primary IEEE record

metadata_notes: CVF verifies pages 9304–9313. Secondary indexes give a different IEEE pagination; an IEEE page range was not verified from the primary record, so the DOI-based IEEE entry deliberately omits pages.

entries.title: TIDE: A General Toolbox for Identifying Object Detection Errors
entries.ieee_entry: D. Bolya, S. Foley, J. Hays, and J. Hoffman, “TIDE: A general toolbox for identifying object detection errors,” in Computer Vision – ECCV 2020, Lecture Notes in Computer Science, vol. 12348. Springer, 2020, pp. 558–573, doi: 10.1007/978-3-030-58580-8_33.
entries.supported_claim: TIDE separates sources of object-detection and instance-segmentation error and measures their effects on average precision, encouraging diagnosis beyond a single aggregate score.
entries.limitation: The project's fixed-threshold missed, unmatched, and duplicate counts are not a full reproduction of TIDE's error-oracle analysis, and corner accuracy requires additional metrics.

entries.title: Simple Baselines for Human Pose Estimation and Tracking
entries.ieee_entry: B. Xiao, H. Wu, and Y. Wei, “Simple baselines for human pose estimation and tracking,” in Proc. European Conf. Computer Vision (ECCV), 2018, pp. 466–481. [Online]. Available: https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_ECCV_2018/html/Bin_Xiao_Simple_Baselines_for_ECCV_2018_paper.html
entries.supported_claim: The human-pose baseline averages heatmaps from original and horizontally flipped inputs during testing, providing a direct pose-estimation precedent for flip testing.
entries.limitation: Its heatmap model and human-joint task differ from the project's two-point regression output, so its results do not establish a cassette improvement.

supports: test-time averaging of original and flipped heatmaps

entries.title: PoseFix: Model-Agnostic General Human Pose Refinement Network
entries.venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
entries.ieee_entry: G. Moon, J. Y. Chang, and K. M. Lee, “PoseFix: Model-agnostic general human pose refinement network,” in Proc. IEEE/CVF Conf. Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), 2019, pp. 7773–7781.
entries.supported_claim: Image and initial-pose input can support a separate pose-refinement stage.
entries.limitation: Human-pose benchmark evidence motivates a cassette experiment; it does not establish cassette accuracy.

entries.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
entries.ieee_entry: C. Guo, G. Pleiss, Y. Sun, and K. Q. Weinberger, “On calibration of modern neural networks,” in Proc. 34th Int. Conf. Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of Machine Learning Research, vol. 70, 2017, pp. 1321–1330. [Online]. Available: https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/guo17a.html
entries.supported_claim: Modern neural-network classification scores can be miscalibrated, and temperature scaling improved calibration on the studied classification tasks.
entries.limitation: A calibrated classification confidence is not automatically a probability of satisfying a two-corner pixel tolerance or of a hidden corner being physically observable.

entries.title: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization
entries.ieee_entry: I. Loshchilov and F. Hutter, “Decoupled weight decay regularization,” in Proc. Int. Conf. Learning Representations (ICLR), 2019. [Online]. Available: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.05101
entries.supported_claim: AdamW separates weight decay from adaptive gradient updates.
entries.limitation: The publication motivates the optimizer; the reported cassette training settings and outcomes are project measurements.

entries.title: Human Pose Regression with Residual Log-Likelihood Estimation
entries.venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
entries.ieee_entry: J. Li et al., “Human pose regression with residual log-likelihood estimation,” in Proc. IEEE/CVF Int. Conf. Computer Vision (ICCV), 2021, pp. 11025–11034.
entries.supported_claim: Residual log-likelihood estimation models coordinate-regression residuals through a likelihood objective.
entries.limitation: Its human-pose results do not establish calibrated five-pixel confidence or cassette performance.

entries.title: Better Aggregation in Test-Time Augmentation
entries.venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
entries.ieee_entry: D. Shanmugam, D. Blalock, G. Balakrishnan, and J. Guttag, “Better aggregation in test-time augmentation,” in Proc. IEEE/CVF Int. Conf. Computer Vision (ICCV), 2021, pp. 1214–1223. [Online]. Available: https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/ICCV2021/html/Shanmugam_Better_Aggregation_in_Test-Time_Augmentation_ICCV_2021_paper.html
entries.supported_claim: In classification, test-time augmentation with standard averaging can turn correct predictions into errors, making aggregation choice and paired-case analysis relevant to evaluation.
entries.limitation: The paper does not evaluate cassette detection or pose fusion and does not justify training an aggregation selector on the small, reused validation set.

entries.title: Human Pose Estimation with Iterative Error Feedback
entries.venue: IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
entries.ieee_entry: J. Carreira, P. Agrawal, K. Fragkiadaki, and J. Malik, “Human pose estimation with iterative error feedback,” in Proc. IEEE Conf. Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), 2016, pp. 4733–4742, doi: 10.1109/CVPR.2016.512.
entries.supported_claim: Image content and a rendered current pose can inform learned coordinate corrections.
entries.limitation: The proposed single-step cassette residual pilot is an adaptation; it does not reproduce the full iterative training scheme or establish cassette accuracy.
